messages:
raj: Thinking out loud — proposal to split the private control-plane handshake into two phases: 1) lightweight auth+connect (agentless-friendly) and 2) full capability negotiation (feature flags, egress policy). Reason: reduce blast radius when onboarding and speed up retry windows. Thoughts?

maggie: I like separating them. Biggest concern is auth token lifecycle — if phase1 issues short-lived creds for phase2, we need a refresh path that survives network hiccups.

alex: agree with maggie. also need to consider path where phase1 succeeds but phase2 times out — we can't leave half-configured routes. Need an idempotent rollback. :thinking: 

sam: what does rollout look like? can we dual-run the old handshake and new split in parallel and compare metrics?

raj: plan is canary split per region. phase1 always backwards compatible (accept old agent tokens). phase2 will be opt-in via capability flag from control plane. rollback = treat phase2 failure as non-fatal and keep existing routing.

jess: ops checklist: make sure we emit clear events for 1->2 transitions. current logs are a mess. Maybe introduce audit event "cp.handshake.phase2.started/finished/failed".

alex: also think about DNS and private endpoint binding timing. If phase1 returns endpoint=10.x.y.z but phase2 needs certs rotated, we need to avoid traffic being sent before certs are ready. 

raj: good call — add a READY gate in phase2 that only flips after certs & iptables rules applied. phase1 will advertise a provisional endpoint and a readiness flag: {ready:false}. Example:
```
phase1 response: { endpoint: "10.10.5.3", token: "short-abc", ready: false }
phase2 -> completes setup -> controlplane patches ready:true
```

maggie: does this change peering assumptions? If we advertise provisional endpoints, consumers might try to connect and get resets. We should document the provisional state in SDKs so retries backoff differently.

alex: SDK change is ok. Also propose server-side backpressure: if many phase2 requests queued, return 429 with Retry-After so agents don't thrash.

sam: testing: create an integration harness that simulates slow cert issuance and toggles peering flaps. We'll need synthetic workloads to catch race conditions.

jess: infra-bot: create a ticket and a deploy playbook stub please.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-1427: "Split CP handshake - phase gating + readiness events". Assigned to @raj. Playbook stub added to /ops/playbooks/handshake-split.md :white_check_mark:

raj: thanks. next steps: write a short RFC addendum with sequence diagrams, define phase2 idempotency semantics, and draft SDK readiness behavior. I'll start the addendum and ping folks for review.

maggie: I'll prototype the token refresh flow (rotate path + offline renewal).

alex: I'll add 429 semantics to the runtime router and a small counter metric for phase2 queue length.

sam: I'll own canary plan + integration tests.

jess: ops will add the event filters and dashboard widgets.

raj: cool — aim to sync again after RFC addendum, target low-risk canary in two sprints. :thumbsup:
